findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_patches, get_change_record, reroll_patch, search_code · Private data: check_patches, describe_dataset, get_change_record, list_change_records, list_class_relations, list_projects, list_symbol_users, lookup_core_symbol, project_profile, project_upgrade_report, reroll_patch, scan_composer, search_code, subsystem_coupling · Public sink: check_patches, project_profile, reroll_patch, scan_composer · Destructive: check_patches, describe_dataset, query_dataset, reroll_patch, subsystem_coupling.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_patches, get_change_record, reroll_patch, search_code · Private data: check_patches, describe_dataset, get_change_record, list_change_records, list_class_relations, list_projects, list_symbol_users, lookup_core_symbol, project_profile, project_upgrade_report, reroll_patch, scan_composer, search_code, subsystem_coupling · Public sink: check_patches, project_profile, reroll_patch, scan_composer · Destructive: check_patches, describe_dataset, query_dataset, reroll_patch, subsystem_coupling

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
